location: /projects · TOP WISHES table row · inline edit chips (type/status/priority/+attach)
problem: Inline row controls are 15–21 px tall, below WCAG 2.2's 24×24 minimum target size. Specifically: WARBAND chip 64×18, +attach 57×17, WISHLIST 77×21, Medium 47×17, column-header sort buttons 29×15. Mis-taps will be common on mobile and for users with motor difficulties.
fix: Bump inline chip and column-sort minimum hit-area to 24×24 — easiest is wrap the visual chip in a button with `min-h-[24px] min-w-[24px]` plus padding, or add `padding: 6px 8px` to lift them above the threshold without altering the visual chip.

principle: NN/g Heuristic 1 (Visibility of system status) + Heuristic 2 (Match between system and real world)
problem: Typing a name like 'Skaven Pestilens Warband' silently strips 'Warband' from the title and assigns it as the project TYPE tag. The user sees a project named 'Skaven Pestilens' with a WARBAND chip — but they never asked for that parse. This is a 'silent magic' moment that violates feedback principle #1 (the system altered input without acknowledging it). New recruits won't know why their name changed.
fix: When the type-parser detects a suffix keyword (warband/army/unit/x20 etc.), either (a) show a one-line preview under the input — 'Will create: Skaven Pestilens · WARBAND' — before they click ADD, or (b) keep the full name and just tag the type without stripping the word, or (c) make the parse opt-in via a checkbox next to the input.

principle: WCAG 2.2 §1.4.10 Reflow + NN/g #4 Consistency (mobile pattern parity)
problem: Top Wishes table and PAINTS wishlist table both fall into horizontal-scroll mode on mobile — visible inner scrollbar appears at the bottom of the table. Columns COMPLETION/0%, OPEN IN ▾ dropdown, and full STATUS label are clipped off-screen. The pattern works (not broken) but it forces a sideways pan to see anything past the first three columns. This is the deferred R7-020 surfacing again under realistic recruit testing.
fix: On <md viewport, swap the project-row + wishlist-row tables for stacked card layout: primary content (name + type chip + status pill) top, progress bar full-width, secondary metadata (priority, OPEN IN, completion %) as a horizontal flex row below. Each row card becomes a tap target of its own.

location: Layout-level — status bar at top + telemetry block at bottom of sidebar shifts position between pages
problem: The bottom-of-sidebar `V0.1.0 // STABLE / R recruit_r8 / ONLINE` block sits at y=638 on /projects but y=663 on /library between navigations. The top status bar (SYS·OK | NET·ON/LAG | TIME) flips NET between ON (green) and LAG (amber) during navigation. Cumulative Layout Shift is visible to the user. This is the still-deferred R7-014/023.
fix: Pin the bottom telemetry block with `position: sticky; bottom: 0` or give the sidebar `display: grid` with a `1fr auto` row layout so the telemetry always lives in the last row. Stabilize the NET indicator by debouncing the `LAG` state for a minimum 1.5s so brief saves don't flip it.

location: /library table columns 'T' and 'OWN' and the hex-row dot
problem: Single-letter column headers 'T' (paint type) and 'OWN' (own/inventory flag) and the unlabelled orange/green/cyan dot next to each hex value force the user to remember what those map to. The legend exists only when the FILTERS panel is expanded — at default view it's hidden. New recruits will not know what the dot or the columns mean.
fix: Add `title` (tooltip) + `aria-label` on the column header buttons ('T' → 'Type (paint/wash/metallic/…)'; 'OWN' → 'Own — toggle inventory'). On the hex dot, add `title="Hue · Orange"` from the same hue-classifier used by the filter. Cheap accessibility + usability win.

principle: Material 3 / Shopify Polaris — categorisation accuracy in auto-classification
problem: Typing 'Citadel Mournfang Brown 18ml' as a manual wishlist entry classified it as category 'OTHER' rather than 'PAINT'. The vendor URL flow probably classifies correctly; the manual-text path doesn't recognise 'Citadel … Brown … ml' as a paint. Recruits who paste 'AK Interactive Sky Blue' won't see it land in their PAINTS section unless they manually fix the category.
fix: When the manual-entry parser sees a vendor-name match against the library brand list (Citadel, Vallejo, AK Interactive, The Army Painter, etc.) AND a `ml` or `fl oz` suffix, default category to PAINT. Keep OTHER as the fallback. Five-line change in the classifier.

principle: Apple HIG — minimum 11pt; Refactoring UI — constrained type scale
location: App-wide — status-bar telemetry, project type chips, tags
problem: Library page samples 17 nodes at 11px (status bar SYS/OK/NET/ON/TIME, sidebar V0.1.0 // STABLE / recruit_r8 / ONLINE). Project page samples 16 nodes including WARBAND and WISHLIST tags. While 11px on monospace is borderline-acceptable for chrome telemetry, the chips are content-level and recruits with normal eyesight in standard zoom may struggle. This is the still-deferred R7-012 — improved (R7 had 59 nodes; v8 ≈ 33 across two pages) but not resolved.
fix: Lift the chip class from `text-[11px]` to `text-xs` (12px) and revisit the telemetry block at 12px too. Or, accept the 11px chrome for terminal aesthetic and lift only the in-content chips (WARBAND, WISHLIST, priority Medium).

problem: Recipe title 'Skaven Verminlord' wraps to 3 lines on iPhone because it's set to a very large display size that doesn't shrink at narrow viewports. Cosmetic, but eats vertical real estate — pushes COLOR SLOTS panel below the fold on first paint.
fix: Add a responsive font-size scale to the h1: `text-3xl md:text-4xl lg:text-5xl` (or whatever Tailwind tokens the app uses) so the recruit-facing first-paint puts the slots panel in view.

problem: Chrome's autofill highlight forces inputs into a pale-blue background with dark text — which clashes visually with the dark terminal theme on every visit until the user types in the field. Functionally accessible; aesthetically incongruous. Recruits will see this on first load.
fix: Style autofill state in CSS: `input:-webkit-autofill { -webkit-box-shadow: 0 0 0 1000px var(--color-surface) inset !important; -webkit-text-fill-color: var(--color-fg) !important; caret-color: var(--color-fg); }`. Standard pattern; eliminates the white-flash.

principle: NN/g Heuristic 9 (Help users recognise, diagnose, recover)
problem: Error pill reads 'WRONG USERNAME OR PASSWORD' — accurate, terminal-flavoured, but doesn't tell a recruit which one was wrong or offer a concrete next step. (Security reasons preclude saying 'username not found' specifically, but adding 'Try again, or use the Forgot password link below' lowers cognitive friction.)
fix: Change to 'Wrong username or password — try again, or hit Forgot password' (still doesn't leak which one was wrong). Keep red border + uppercase if the terminal aesthetic demands it.

location: /tools · breadcrumb `← TOOLS` button at top-left of the tools landing page itself
problem: On `/tools` (the landing page), there's a `← TOOLS` button at top-left even though there's no parent to back up to. It's a back-link that points to itself. Small but disorienting on first visit.
fix: Hide the back-link on the landing page; only render it on `/tools/wheel`, `/tools/match`, `/tools/eyedropper`, `/tools/layering`.

location: Mobile bottom tab bar + top-right avatar
problem: User page is reachable only via top-right avatar tap on mobile (R7-009 fix works). But when on /user, the bottom tab bar shows no active item — Library/Recipes/Tools/Wishlist all look unselected. There's no visual indication of 'where am I?' for the user route.
fix: When on /user, give the top avatar a subtle active treatment (1px cyan ring around the avatar circle, matching the active-tab cyan glow on bottom tabs). Or add a `User` icon as the 5th bottom-tab slot and demote one of the existing 4 — but that's a bigger lift.
